column1: # Lexime curated extras: SI units that stand after a typed digit (3びょう → 3s).
# Format: reading[TAB]surface[TAB]pos[TAB]cost (the curated grammar, as the
# other extras domains; see extras.rs). Every row is 名詞,接尾,助数詞,*,*,*,*
# (Mozc's POS for a unit word); every surface is a pure-Latin counter (ASCII
# letters, no Japanese character), which is what lets the Latin-unit rules
# (Viterbi formation, rerank script price, NumericRewriter) apply. μ is U+03BC
# and ° is U+00B0.
# Cost rule: C = c_ref + rank. c_ref is the cost of the unit's Japanese name
# (same reading, the unit's canonical name — カタカナ, or 摂氏 / 華氏 / 秒 /
# ワット時): among the entries of that (reading, surface) in the built
# dictionary (engine/data/lexime.dict, after compile's role cost correction),
# the cheapest one whose left and right ids are both the unit's own id
# (名詞,接尾,助数詞) if there is one, else the cheapest entry of the surface,
# ids not considered. (Only なのめーとる / ぼると have a cheaper entry under
# another id: ナノメートル 5337 / ボルト 4524; c_ref is 6058 / 4601, the
# same-id entry.) rank is the unit's place among the units of the same
# reading (1, 2, ...): bit = +1, b = +2; every other reading has one unit, +1.
# So a unit sorts right after its Japanese name and never above it.
# A reading Mozc has no Japanese name for (10 readings, marked "derived")
# has its name as a row of unit-names.tsv (名詞,一般, a single entry, so
# c_ref = that row's cost). Its c_ref = the cost of the unit-less base's
# cheapest entry in the built dictionary + the median, over the same-family
# prefixed compounds the dictionary has, of (compound cheapest cost - base
# cheapest cost); an even-n median is floored. The derivation takes each word's cheapest entry (not the same-id
# entry), so for a derived reading c_ref is that derived value and the two
# quantities (c_ref, the cheapest) differ only in nm / V. The readings
# どしー / どえふ are variants of せっし / かし and take the same C as the main
# reading (the same surface is not priced differently by reading).
# Values are counted on the built dictionary (engine/data/lexime.dict, compiled
# from the pin in engine/data/mozc-pin.txt, after compile's role cost
# correction; each word's cheapest entry); when the pin is bumped, derive them
# again. The comment above each reading gives its c_ref (the Japanese name and
# its cost in the built dictionary) or its derivation.
